scientific_question: Do independently dated East-Asian Cirsium lineage divergences repeatedly occur during unusual global eustatic sea-level states or short-window sea-level dynamics?
analysis_scope: lineage-diversification range-reorganization context only; not local island connectivity and not a capitulum-trait transition test

source.dataset: NOAA/WDS Global 5 Million Year Sea Level, Temperature, and d18Osw Reconstructions
source.associated_publication: de Boer et al. 2014 Nature Communications 5:2999

exclusion_reason: Use one representative dated divergence per broad clade group for recurrence. Nested Nipponocirsium nodes are diagnostics, not independent replicates; the 2.4 Ma founder event has different process semantics and a broad source/recipient uncertainty.

age_uncertainty.interpretation: Deterministic scenarios across published marginal age intervals; not posterior samples.

metrics.sea_level_state: sea level at the candidate node age
metrics.window_mean: mean sea level within the fixed short window
metrics.window_sd: temporal SD within the fixed short window
metrics.window_range: max minus min sea level within the fixed short window
metrics.endpoint_abs_change: absolute sea-level difference across the fixed short window
metrics.mean_abs_1k_change: mean absolute 1-kyr sea-level change within the fixed short window
metrics.max_abs_1k_change: maximum absolute 1-kyr sea-level change within the fixed short window

robustness_rules.low_or_high_state: For sea_level_state and window_mean, low requires event-age percentile q95 <= 0.10 and high requires q05 >= 0.90 in both background horizons. For window_mean the same class must also hold for both 50- and 100-kyr windows.
robustness_rules.high_dynamic_metric: For SD, range, endpoint absolute change, mean absolute 1-kyr change and max absolute 1-kyr change, require event-age percentile q05 >= 0.90 in both background horizons and for both 50- and 100-kyr windows.
robustness_rules.recurring_context_candidate: A sea-level context is a descriptive recurring lineage-differentiation opportunity if the same robust class occurs in at least two of the three predeclared representative clade groups. Three of three is stronger. No p-value is assigned.

claim_boundary: Global eustatic sea level is a range-reorganization context variable, not a reconstruction of local Taiwan/Ryukyu/Japan land connectivity.
A low sea-level or high-dynamic result would identify an isolation/connectivity opportunity only; it would not identify a selective pressure on a capitulum trait.
Published lineage-divergence ages are not capitulum-trait transition ages.
Age scenarios are deterministic uncertainty grids, not independent events or posterior draws.
No result from this internal diagnostic is required to appear in the final manuscript.
A lineage-level range context cannot substitute for a missing trait-specific historical trigger.
